markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Normal (83%)** · Ambiguous: Normal vs InSitu · Careful review
InSitu (12%) stays in the 90% set on this blurred frozen section.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Normal 83%, InSitu 12%, Invasive 4%, Benign 1% [F1] | Favors Normal; low invasive risk |
| Conformal set | Normal, InSitu (90% target; 90% test coverage) | Includes InSitu at 90% |
| Reliability / OOD | 96% reliability, 86% OOD, 12/12 regions [F6] | Passes QC despite blur |
| CONCH–MUSK agreement | True (same top class) | Independent models agree |
| Similar cases | 5/5 Normal (85%–86%) [F5]; InSitu contrast 83% | Neighbors Normal; close InSitu |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules with two-layered epithelium** (regions 1, 2, 8) · ↓ invasive · Above-typical (-0.795) [F2]; 0/20 spot check · Unreliable
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 2, 7, 9) · ↓ invasive · Above-typical (-0.64) [F3]; 20/20 spot check · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (region 9) · ↑ invasive · Scarce (-1.336, +0.514) [F4]; 12/20 spot check · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Faithful; deleting top-3 risk regions drops invasive score above random (0.0114, 95% CI 0.0021–0.0197).
- **Concepts**: Unproven (deletion CI -0.0088–0.0064 includes 0); top concept normal_lobules (-0.795) is Unreliable (0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- Severity-3 blur on this simulated frozen section masks InSitu (12%; contrast BACH_0043 83% similar).
- Unsampled levels harbor atypia or InSitu (deeper levels drafted; stains blocked on frozen sections).

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 3, 0, 8**: Highest regional risk (0.015, 0.002); inspect blurred epithelium and consider drafted deeper levels.
2. **Regions 9, 10**: Inspect ducts and tubules distinguishing Normal from InSitu contrast BACH_0043.
3. **Regions 1, 2, 7**: Visually verify lobules (Unreliable concept) and clear margins (medial 81%, superior 79%) [F7].

found: The CONCH–MUSK row names Normal, but agreement.conch_musk_same_top only says the two models agree with each other; the JSON does not say which class they chose.
